name: Tarsus
overview: Tarsus is prominently identified in Scripture as the birthplace of Paul, a significant figure in the early church, described as a notable city in Cilicia (Acts 21:39; 22:3). After Paul's conversion, believers sent him from Jerusalem to Tarsus to protect him from those seeking to harm him (Acts 9:30). Later, Barnabas traveled to Tarsus to bring Paul to Antioch, where they ministered together and helped establish the church that first bore the name Christian (Acts 11:25-26). These passages highlight Tarsus not only as Paul's hometown but also as a place integral to his early ministry and the spread of the gospel.
